§ 49. I had almost forgotten to mention that another author of this very same character (namely John Pordage) has been published; although he likely drew great benefit from reading this author <note>Arnold is referring to Jacob Böhme here, as Pordage was a well-known follower of Böhme's philosophy.</note>, he was nonetheless nourished by the very same source, such that he was led perhaps even deeper into it. Chap. II. Of spiritual knowledge: essential, figurative, and rational, belonging to both the brain and the heart; how one should conduct oneself toward such knowledge as well as toward the experiences of others. The basis of the divine authority of the Holy Scripture. <note>This chapter likely addresses the distinction between intellectual "head-knowledge" and the "heart-knowledge" prized by mystics.</note>

III. Of the Spirit of Eternity: that such a spirit exists, and what it is.

IV. Of the Spirit of Eternity, considered as unrevealed. <note>This refers to God or the Absolute in its "hidden" state before creation or self-manifestation.</note>

VI. Further consideration of the Spirit of Eternity in relation to its revelation through essential emanations <note>original: *Ausflüsse*; a central concept in mystical thought where the universe "flows out" from God's own being.</note>, births, and creatures: And first, of an un-emanated divine world, its possibility, diversity, and the creatures found within it.

VII. Of the emanated divine world, called by Dr. Pordage the Sphere of Eternity; and of the diversity of creatures arising from it: Matter, Life, Death, etc. <note>Pordage’s "Sphere of Eternity" represents the first stage of spiritual manifestation where pure ideas and spiritual beings reside.</note>

VIII. Of Eternal Nature, and the other worlds that follow.

# Table of Chapters.

**Chap. II.** From what motive, to what end, and in what state or condition of heart he brought his spiritual experiences to light. <note>John Pordage was known for his intense visions; here he explains why he felt compelled to share these private mystical encounters with the public.</note>

**III.** What the author thinks of the Holy Scripture.

**IV.** Several descriptions or interpretations of certain words. <note>This chapter likely serves as a glossary for the specialized mystical vocabulary used by the author.</note>

**V.** **Dr. Pordage’s** agreement with **Jakob Böhme**, and his high esteem for him. <note>Jakob Böhme (1575–1624) was a German shoemaker and mystic whose writings on the nature of God and the soul became the foundation for "Behmenism," which Pordage championed in England.</note>

**VI.** Depiction of **Dr. Pordage’s** system <note>original: "Systema"</note> or order of the world. <note>This refers to Pordage’s complex map of the spiritual universe, often involving diagrams of the "emanations" or layers of reality.</note>

**VII.** The first opening of the invisible world shared with the author. <note>In mystical literature, an "opening" is a moment of divine revelation where the spiritual realm becomes visible to the internal sight.</note>

**VIII.** The effects of these first openings: The Virginal Life. <note>The "Virginal Life" refers to a state of spiritual purity and devotion, often seeking a mystical union with "Divine Sophia" or Wisdom rather than earthly marriage.</note>

**IX.** Why **Dr. Pordage** kept these first openings secret for so long?

**X.** **Dr. Pordage’s** defense regarding appealing to a higher secular authority, and preaching for a salary. <note>Pordage was a controversial figure who was eventually ejected from his rectory at Bradfield on charges of heresy and pantheism; this chapter addresses the practical and legal fallout of his ministry.</note>

# Chapter I.
## Of Spirit in General: That a Spirit exists: What it is: And some of its essential properties.

->§. 1.<-

<margin>General concept of a spirit, from</margin>
Experience convinces us that many **bodies** or **physical forms** <note>original: "Leiber oder Cörper". In the 17th century, these terms often distinguished between the living body and the material substance.</note> are moved.

<margin>Contemplation of bodily motion.</margin>
§. 2. Just as there is undoubtedly a motion, so there is also a **moving power**, and something that is moved.

§. 3. Moving is an **effect** <term>effect: original "Würckung", implying an active influence or operation</term>, a doing; and being moved is a **passion** <term>passion: original "Leiden", meaning the state of being acted upon or receiving an action, rather than emotional suffering</term>.

§. 4. The moving power then is an **active** being, but the moved body is a **passive** being, with respect to one and the same motion.

§. 5. Acting and passion are two opposing or contra- <note>The text cuts off here at the end of the page; the prefix "wider-" likely completes as "widersinnig" (contrary) or "widerstrebend" (conflicting) on the following page.</note>

<summary>In this opening chapter, Pordage establishes a logical proof for the existence of spirit by observing the physical world, arguing that since bodies move, there must be a distinct "active power" or spirit that initiates that movement.</summary>
<keywords>spirit, motion, active power, passive being, natural philosophy, metaphysics, John Pordage</keywords>

### Introduction / I. B.

<margin><insert><unclear>Extension is no Substance</unclear></insert></margin>
The principal cause of all doubts raised in this matter, in my opinion, is that the learned gentlemen have taken it upon themselves to provide a definition or formal description of **extension** <term>the quality of taking up or stretching through space</term> that was intended to express its very nature. And so they claimed that **extension** consists in a thing having parts placed alongside other parts (a); this is an entirely false description, as would be any other that one might attempt to formulate. For the **extension** or stretching out of a thing in height, depth, length, and width is such a simple and universally known **notion** <term>original: *Notion*; a fundamental concept or mental grasp</term> or understanding, that it is impossible to find anything simpler or clearer which might serve to make the concept one has of **extension** even more luminous and intelligible than it already is in and of itself. Consequently, anything one might say about it can only serve to make it that much more obscure and incomprehensible.

## Recognizing the things of God as they truly are, so that one may love Him deeply.

<margin>The vanity of filling the head even with true images.</margin>

### Glorification and Transformation of the lower through the higher things: As we wish to show in sequence, yet briefly.

**§. 39.** Firstly then, because the **Spirit of Eternity** is an infinite fullness of **Power** <note>original: "Krafft." In this context, it refers to divine energy or potentiality.</note>, and at the same time a perfect **Freedom**, He can proceed out of Himself in infinite variety, and extend His most holy **outflows** as little or as far as He pleases, without measure or limit.

**§. 40.** We must be content if, according to the narrowness of our understanding, we may perceive some types of this infinite variety of His **outflows**. ### VIII. C. Eternal Nature.

...[immateria]l, or exist without any corporeality; and whether the capacity to think, as well as to be conscious of one’s own thoughts and actions, can only exist within a pure, simple spirit <note>original: "einwesigten Geist," referring to a spirit of a single, unified essence rather than one made of parts</note>?

<margin>
Answer.
</margin>
I answer: We do not perfectly know the nature of the **Eternal Elements**; and therefore we cannot prove that thinking and being self-conscious cannot exist alongside them. That these powers—although in a lower degree—are found in composite beings, is proven in **Chapter XII** of this treatise through the example of animals. Previously, I have demonstrated that **matter** is nothing other than spiritual, congealed powers <note>original: "zusammengeronnene Kräffte," suggesting a process like curdling or coagulation where spiritual energy becomes dense substance</note>. Therefore, even though pure, simple spirits are not composed of the four elements, their subjective, constituent essence—from which they are made—still contains within itself the same powers found in the four elements, only in a finer and higher degree of being, and inseparably. If, then, simple spirits are endowed with these powers, as is indeed the case, then the **Eternal Elements** can also be endowed with them.

# VIII. C. Archaei of the Other Worlds.

<margin>
The Archaeus of this world is rational.
</margin>
...this **visible** world, GOTT <note>The author uses the capitalized "GOTT" for God.</note> brought forth and created its spirit or <term>Archaeus</term> <note>original Latin: *Archæum*. In this context, it refers to the "world-soul" or the vital organizing force of the physical universe.</note> from a portion of the matter that had been corrupted by **Lucifer**. Our author, as well as several others, states that this spirit of the world is a rational spirit.

However, I do not believe it is their meaning that its reason is identical to human reason. This is because human reason has united within itself the highest, simple, understanding spirit, which stems from eternity and works in, with, and through that reason; by this, human reason is greatly elevated in its effects. But the spirit of this world has no such high, simple, eternal spirit united with it.

### XII. C. The Immensity of God.

[It] relates how the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord as a cloud, so that the priests could not see or perform their duties because of the cloud; and upon this Solomon said: 

> The Lord has spoken: He would dwell in the darkness. I have built a house as a dwelling for Thee, a seat, that Thou mayest dwell there eternally.

Thereupon, in the 27th verse, he raises an objection to himself:

### XII. C. System of the Ancient Hebrews.

<margin>Followers of the Infinite <note>original Latin: *En-sophici*, referring to those who study the *Ein Sof*, the infinite divine essence.</note>.</margin>
...[The] Basic Being with its understanding has formed and shaped the **System** out of free will / which is truly the beginning and origin of all produced things; and which God (according to the opinion of the **Kabbalists**) has impressed like a seal upon that space / which was destined for the creatures and divine revelations.

The ten upper lights of **Adam Kadmon** <note>Hebrew: "Primordial Man." In Kabbalah, this is the first spiritual manifestation of the Infinite light, serving as a blueprint for all of creation.</note> itself are the (a) ideal powers <note>original Latin: *virtutes ideales*</note> of the Holy Trinity and of the seven spirits of God / which are contained within that same wisdom.

The withdrawal or contraction <note>This refers to the concept of *Tzimtzum*, where God "contracted" His infinite light to create a "vacuum" or space in which finite creation could exist.</note> of the glory of the **Infinite**, and the first space / is the (b) secondary essence <note>original Latin: *secundaria essentia*</note> of God / moderated according to the (c) receptivity of the creatures <note>original Latin: *attemperata ad statum receptibilitatis Creaturarum*</note> / and (d) informed <note>original Latin: *informata*, meaning to be given an inner form or soul</note> or animated with the (e) schematic wisdom <note>original Latin: *sapientiâ sciagraphicâ*, referring to a preliminary outline or structural draft of wisdom.</note>.

The channel is the center of this entire (f) **Infinite** <note>The text uses the term *Æn-sophisch*, derived from the Hebrew *Ein Sof* (Without End).</note> world / the primary seat of the schematic and prototypical wisdom / from whence life / movement and all revelations emerge.

### III. C. and the Outer Man.

...of **God** / *God’s dwelling place* <note>original: "Dei locus"</note>, as the translator has quite rightly rendered it. And although in this German copy, near the end of the aforementioned sermon, the outer and the rational man are called **two states** <note>original: "duo status"</note>: it is nevertheless sure and certain that Tauler does not mean a threefold "state" in the proper sense—that is, a threefold condition, property, or state of one and the same **substance** <term>Substanz: the underlying essence or core of a thing that remains the same even if its appearance changes</term> and being. 

For such threefold conditions and properties are not present in every person, nor can they exist simultaneously in anyone; yet Tauler affirms that they do. Furthermore, I do not see how the word **disposition** <note>original: "Habitus", a philosophical term for a person's characteristic state or tendency</note>, or condition, can be called a **human being** <note>original: "Homo"</note>. Therefore, Tauler here understands three distinct parts which constitute the whole person as he is currently composed. For he himself, in this sermon, calls the rational man a "part" of the human being when he says: "In that part, the human being is lord over all bodily **creatures** <note>original: "Creaturen"</note>." In the same way, he also calls the innermost man the **innermost ground of the soul**, where **God’s** throne is located—

It is rooted in the fire-spirit, in the fourth form of nature <note>referring to the fourth of Böhme's Seven Properties of Nature</note>, whereas **Wisdom** is born from the fifth [form], the Light. Section 57.

**Numbers or Sephiroth** <term>Sephiroth: the ten attributes or emanations in Jewish Kabbalah through which the Infinite is revealed</term>, the three most distinguished and highest. Book 12, Section 143, number 3. These are the highest: the Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding <note>original: *Klugheit*, here corresponding to the Sephirah *Binah*</note>; they are also called the three minds <note>original Latin: *tres mentes*</note>. Same place and following, Section 145. They are types <note>original: *Vorbildchens*, small prefigurations</note> of the Holy Trinity: the Eye, the Heart, and the Holy Spirit. Same place, Section 144. Look for **General Ideas** <note>original Latin: *Idee generales*</note>. . . . The seven lower numbers. Book 12, Section 143, number 5 and following. They correspond with the seven spirits of God. Same place, Section 144 . . . They are words. Book 12, Section 146, number 29. What they are. number 30. They are not creatures. number 31. Everything relates to the Sephiroth. number 32.
